nodes.title: Export AI chat conversations to a Markdown file from supported platforms
Keep new-platform support cheap: one primary selector plus text fallbacks per site
Per-turn copy buttons are the only reliable, load-bearing selectors for extraction
Index-based alternation from a user-first conversation reliably classifies turn roles
copyButtonSelector

detail.definition: The per-platform CSS selector matching each conversation turn's native copy button; the single required, load-bearing selector for extraction.

nodes.title: SiteConfig

detail.definition: The per-platform selector bundle (copy/message/title/edit selectors plus a conversation-path matcher) keyed by Site.

nodes.title: Diagnostic report

detail.definition: The JSON health report produced by Verify Export, recording selector counts, extraction results, detected issues, and a health level.

nodes.title: Target platforms are ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity conversation pages
Chat-platform DOMs change frequently and break structural selectors
Extraction must succeed when copy buttons are present and fail clearly when they are absent
Turn-level copy buttons must be separated from nested code-block copy buttons
Each extracted turn must be classified as a user or assistant turn
Clipboard capture must fall back to DOM text extraction when it fails
Adding a platform must require only a working copyButtonSelector and text fallbacks
Export must download Markdown with title, source URL, timestamp, and XML-style turn markers
Verify Export must produce a downloadable JSON diagnostics report and an in-page health badge
(Retired) Discard code-block copy buttons by testing button.closest("pre, code")
Conversations always start with a user turn
Turn-level copy buttons sit at a consistent DOM depth across all matched buttons
Prefer data-testid attributes; avoid Tailwind/utility classes as selectors
Avoid deeply structural selectors that depend on nesting or sibling relationships
Even-indexed copy buttons are user turns; odd-indexed are assistant turns
The depth filter and alternation logic are platform-agnostic; only the copyButtonSelector and text fallbacks are platform-specific
Use native copy buttons as the primary extraction path

detail.chosen_option: Extract turn text by clicking each turn's native copy button and reading the clipboard
rejected: Scrape message DOM nodes as the primary path
detail.rationale: Native copy actions are explicitly maintained by each platform and yield clean, canonical message text.

nodes.title: Filter turn buttons by modal DOM depth instead of button.closest("pre, code")

detail.chosen_option: Keep copy buttons whose DOM depth is within a small tolerance of the modal depth across all matches
rejected: Test each button with button.closest('pre, code')
detail.rationale: A platform-agnostic depth filter discards nested code-block copy buttons without brittle structural checks.

nodes.title: Classify turn roles primarily by index alternation, with hints only confirming

detail.chosen_option: Classify turns by button index parity (even=user, odd=assistant) and use platform hints only to confirm
rejected: Rely on data-testid or aria role hints as the primary classifier
detail.rationale: Conversations always start with a user turn, so index parity is universal while hints are platform-specific and often absent.

nodes.title: On a supported page, every classified turn yields non-empty extracted text via clipboard or fallback
A code-block copy button nested deep inside an assistant response that must be discarded
